recentItems.title: Famed Nunawading Studios Open for Business Again
recentItems.description:
Famed Nunawading Studios Open for Business Again

The famed Nunawading television studios — once home to some of Australia’s most iconic programs including Neighbours, Prisoner, Young Talent Time and Rove Live — are officially open for business again.

Now known as The Studio Forest Hill, the site was decommissioned last September after Fremantle Australia vacated the facility.

But like a phoenix, the studios have been given a new lease on life, with Matt Batten and TV City now helping drive a new vision for the site.
And the cameras are already rolling.

A major feature film has been shooting at the studios for the past four months, making extensive use of the facilities, while interest from other productions continues to grow.

Studio A and Studio B comprise some of the largest television studio spaces in Melbourne outside of Docklands Studios. The site also offers production offices, extensive storage facilities and additional spaces suitable for film, television and content production.

Batten says momentum is building quickly, with bookings already filling across the remainder of 2026.

“It’s fantastic to see a major production shooting here and activity returning to the studios. We’re now receiving strong interest from other productions, and the remainder of the year is quickly booking out.”

“The Studio is purpose-built to take your project from concept to screen seamlessly. We have the studio space, offices, storage and facilities all in the one location, and we’re excited about what’s ahead.”

With a major film already in production and bookings filling for the remainder of the year, The Studio Forest Hill is once again becoming a busy Melbourne production hub.

recentItems.title: TV City Episode 81 Interview with Paul Kelman
recentItems.description:
Episode 81 – Paul Kelman (Chris Patchett – E Street)

In Episode 81 of the TV City Podcast, Matt Batten sits down with actor Paul Kelman, best known for playing the popular character Chris Patchett on the iconic Australian drama E Street.

In this in-depth interview, Paul reflects on his life and acting career, sharing fascinating behind-the-scenes stories from the set of E Street. He talks about landing the role of Chris Patchett, working alongside the cast, what it was like during the show's most successful years, and why he ultimately decided to leave the series.

Paul also discusses life after E Street, his career beyond the show, and shares plenty of memories that fans have never heard before.

If you're an E Street fan or love classic Australian television, this is an interview you won't want to miss.

recentItems.title: TV City Episode 80 - Interview with Pete Smith
recentItems.description:
Episode 80 – Pete Smith 

TV City host Matt Batten sits down with the legendary Pete Smith to talk about his extraordinary career in radio and television.

In this special episode, Matt and Pete chat about Pete’s childhood, the golden days of radio and TV, and of course his iconic time on In Melbourne Tonight.

Pete also shares how he landed the role on Sale of the Century, along with incredible behind-the-scenes stories from one of Australia’s most loved television eras.

From the golden days of Australian television to life today, this is a fascinating and nostalgic conversation with one of the true legends of the industry.

A must-watch for anyone who loves classic Australian TV.

recentItems.title: Corals Soapbox with Coral Drouyn and Matt Batten Episode 79
recentItems.description:
Welcome to another episode of Coral's Soapbox with legendary television writer and producer Coral Drouyn and TV City host Matt Batten.

Each week, Coral and Matt sit down to discuss everything television, entertainment and the stories making headlines both in Australia and around the world.

In this episode, the pair talk TV news, world news, behind-the-scenes stories from the television industry and some of their favourite Australian television shows, including Prisoner, Neighbours, Home and Away, Arcade, Paradise Beach and many more.

Drawing on Coral's decades of experience in the television industry, the conversation offers unique insights into the people, productions and moments that helped shape Australian television history.

Plus, Coral and Matt make a special announcement that fans won't want to miss.

recentItems.title: TV City - Interview with Peter Vroom - Lance Smart Home and Away Early Years Episode 78
recentItems.description:
TV City host Matt Batten sits down for an exclusive interview with Peter Vroom, best known to Australian television audiences as Lance Smart from the iconic soap opera Home and Away.

Peter joined the series from Episode 1, making Lance one of the show's original characters and a familiar face to millions of viewers throughout the early years of Summer Bay.

In this fascinating interview, Peter shares the story of how he landed the role, including the audition process that saw him bring the lovable and often naïve Lance to life. We also discuss what it was like being part of a brand-new television series that would go on to become one of Australia's most successful television exports.

Peter reflects on working alongside some of the show's most beloved cast members, including Lyn Collingwood, Ray Meagher, Roger Oakley, Kate Ritchie and many more. He also shares plenty of behind-the-scenes stories from the early days of Home and Away, offering fans a unique insight into life on set during the show's formative years.

We also catch up with Peter's life after acting, including his successful career in mediation and his life today in Los Angeles.

If you're a fan of classic Home and Away, Australian television history or simply enjoy hearing incredible stories from the people who helped shape Australian TV, this is an interview you won't want to miss.

Please like, subscribe and share to help us continue preserving Australia's rich television history through TV City.

recentItems.title: TV City - Interview with Peter Ford – Inside His Life & the World of Entertainment Episode 77
recentItems.description:
TV City host and producer Matt Batten sits down with one of Australia’s most respected entertainment reporters for a rare and in-depth conversation.

Peter Ford rarely gives interviews — but in this exclusive, Matt spends over 90 minutes with him, diving into his incredible career and life behind the headlines.

In this episode, Peter opens up about his move to the Gold Coast, his childhood and early life, and how he started in radio as an office boy before working his way into the entertainment industry. He shares insights into his work across radio and television, the biggest stories he has broken, and what his day really looks like behind the scenes, from early starts to deciding which stories to run.

He also talks about how the media and entertainment industry has changed over the years, the impact of social media, and reflects on his close friendship with the late Bert Newton.

This is a fascinating and honest look inside the world of showbiz from someone who has truly seen it all.

recentItems.title: Corals Soapbox with Coral Drouyn and Matt Batten Episode 76
recentItems.description:
Welcome to another episode of Corals Soapbox, where Coral Drouyn, a seasoned veteran of Australian television, delves into the depths of iconic TV shows. Coral's extensive resume includes work on beloved series like Neighbours, Home and Away, and, notably, Prisoner. As a script writer, Script Editor, Story Liner, and Story Editor on Prisoner, Coral shaped some of the show's most memorable characters and storylines.

Talking Prisoner Host Matt Batten sits down with legendary writer Coral Drouyn for another episode of Coral’s Soapbox, filmed live from Ballarat.
This is a huge episode.

Coral selects her favourite fan-submitted storyline from the Talking Prisoner Facebook page and reads it directly to the fans — bringing the audience into the creative process like never before.
In this exclusive episode, Coral also reveals how she would have brought back Bea Smith and ended the iconic series Prisoner — sharing the powerful storyline she would have written if Bea had returned.

This is a Talking Prisoner exclusive, packed with behind-the-scenes insight and never-before-heard ideas from one of the key creatives behind the show.
A must-watch for any Prisoner fan.

recentItems.title: Talking Prisoner – Episode 73: Interview with Ric Herbert (Andy Hudson)
recentItems.description:
Talking Prisoner – Episode 73: Interview with Ric Herbert (Andy Hudson)

In this episode of Talking Prisoner, host and producer Matt Batten sits down with Ric Herbert, who famously played Andy Hudson in Prisoner (Cell Block H).

Joining via Zoom from Canada, Ric and Matt chat for over an hour about Ric’s life growing up, his remarkable career in acting and voice-over work, and his extensive television credits, including:

Rescue Special Ops, Underbelly: A Tale of Two Cities, Home and Away, Wildside, All Saints, Police Rescue, The Young Doctors, TV Follies (ABC), The Sullivans, A Country Practice, Prisoner, Sweet & Sour (ABC) and many more.

Ric also opens up about his life living in Canada, how he landed the role of Andy Hudson on Prisoner, his close friendship with Anna Hruby (Pattie Lawson), and shares plenty of behind-the-scenes stories from the iconic series.

Beyond acting, Ric is one of Australia’s most prolific voice artists. He joined RMK, Australia’s premium voice agency, in 1980 and has since been employed over 14,000 times for voice-over work. Chances are, you’ve eaten breakfast, lunch, and dinner with Ric’s voice without even knowing it.

Starting out as “Ricky the Boy,” Ric has worked for hundreds of clients — from being the voice of the Nesquik Bunny to promos for ABC, XYZ, Cartoon Network, and the Sci-Fi Channel. His animation credits include 14 films for Burbank and multiple voices across 52 episodes of Little Horrors for December Films.

Among countless other credits, Ric is currently the voice of Channel 7’s X Factor.

A must-watch episode packed with stories, nostalgia, and insight into one of Australia’s most recognisable voices.
